task:
Extend the saved urllib.parse library's regression tests and reference documentation for port access on the results of urlsplit and urlparse. The checked-out implementation is the authority for existing behavior; do not change it.

In Lib/test/test_urlparse.py, add regression coverage for both public functions with text URLs and ASCII byte URLs: no port, an empty port, 0, 65535, 65536, a negative port, and a noninteger port. Also cover non-ASCII decimal digits in text URLs. Establish when invalid-port errors occur, and assert the exact exception class, complete argument tuple and diagnostic text. Assert the concrete results for accepted boundary cases. Keep all existing tests and supporting source intact.

In Doc/library/urllib.parse.rst, add a focused explanation and executable examples of the observed boundary/error behavior, including the distinction between constructing the parsed result and accessing its port. Preserve every original documentation line byte-for-byte and in its original order: insertions only, with no rewrites or deletions. New examples must be self-contained together (include their imports), use >>> prompts, and show their real outputs or exceptions. Do not copy an untested expectation into the explanation as if saving it established library behavior.

The host runs the tests scope after each accepted test-file edit, and the public scope after each accepted documentation edit. Tests scope runs the saved and edited suite, observes the required API/input paths, and checks that the new tests detect changes to exception class/arguments/message, validation timing and valid boundary values separately at each required API, input type and case. Fault-detection assessment requires a passing ordinary control; mutation runs need not complete all normal path coverage. Examples scope executes the newly added examples. Public includes both scopes and preservation checks. All scopes are available on request. Only a public pass on the current candidate authorizes submission. Documentation prose also receives a separate review after the run.

Start from the supplied saved files, find the relevant source, complete both contributions, use actual feedback, and submit the checked result. Provisional work is permitted; preserve consequential unresolved questions in the optional working account and revise them when evidence changes. A saved expectation is authored work, not an execution observation. This task describes a new contribution in the current session, not a report that a previous session's edit has failed.

assessment.explanation: Ordinary execution and its required path coverage must pass. Fault sensitivity is assessed only with a passing ordinary control, at the declared targets. Mutation-run path completeness is not required. A pass is scoped evidence, not verification of all prose or of the model account.
